Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Immediate: sudden latency spike & 5xx surge impacting HL7 pipeline

Hi team,

We started seeing a significant increase in tail latency and 5xx errors against the Redwood inference endpoint backing our HL7 ingestion between 2027-01-14 22:30 UTC and 2027-01-15 02:10 UTC. Metrics summary from our side: 95th pct latency jumped from ~220ms to ~1.8s, throughput dropped ~40%, and 5xx rate climbed to ~3.5%. This caused backpressure in our downstream ETL and delayed several critical batch jobs for the night window.

We raised a support ticket (SEV2-9938) but need executive attention — this is a revenue-impacting outage window for our clinical uploads. Please escalate; we will need remediation + a commercial remedy given our SLA in section 5.2 of the Master Services Agreement.

Immediate asks:
- Root cause summary and timeline for the incident
- Quantified SLA credit/calculation and when that will be applied
- Short-term mitigation (capacity/throughput) so we don’t recur during our next night window (01/16)
- A time for an exec-to-exec sync if possible today

Thanks,
Samantha Reed
Head of Integrations
Clearwater Health

Subject: Re: Immediate: sudden latency spike & 5xx surge impacting HL7 pipeline — preliminary technical findings

Quick summary from SRE: we saw an atypical KV cache growth after a model variant rollout that increased sequence length variance for a subset of requests. The serving runtime’s batching heuristics ended up backlogging some worker queues under the observed request distribution, leading to increased tokenization/attention overhead and backpressure that manifested as elevated tail latency and cascading 5xxs when workers dropped requests.

Immediate remediation we executed:
- Rolled back the model variant for the affected deployment at 10:20 PST (rollback completed at 10:24).
- Increased pre-warming pool and forced smaller continuous batches for the HL7 route.
- Restarted a subset of worker pods to clear stale KV caches.

Impact: error rate dropped to baseline within ~18 minutes after rollback; 95th pct latency returned to ~250–300ms within 30 minutes. We’ve attached an initial SLO analysis export for your review (slo_analysis.csv).

Follow-ups:
- We will run a targeted traffic replay across a staging patch to ensure the batching adjustments hold for your workload.
- We recommend scheduling a controlled dedicated capacity window if you need guaranteed throughput for the nightly window while we harden the rollout gating.

— Dev
SRE, Redwood Inference
